subject: Decision Making
title: Devil's Advocate Role
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Devil's Advocate Role.

hook.text: The Catholic Church assigned a devil's advocate to argue against sainthood.

buildup.text: In business, a devil's advocate is assigned to attack the team's preferred plan.

discovery.text: Teams with a devil's advocate consider more alternatives and catch more risks than teams without one.

twist.text: The role only works if the advocate genuinely argues. Token dissent that everyone knows is fake has no effect.

climax.text: Structured dissent is more effective than hoping someone will naturally disagree.

punchline.text: Assign someone to disagree. Structured dissent beats hoping for natural.

quiz.question: Why must the devil's advocate role be genuine, not token?
options: Fake dissent that everyone recognizes has no effect on group decision quality
